findings.title: Swallows notification exceptions without logging
findings.explanation: When the notifier raises an exception, the code catches all exceptions and silently discards them, providing no logging or reporting. This hides notification failures and makes debugging difficult, violating proper error handling practices. Also reported by compliance as requirement_mismatch: When notification fails, the exception is silently ignored without any logging, contrary to the requirement that a failed notification be logged for operators. Also reported by standards as maintainability: The code catches a broad Exception and silently ignores it with `pass`, which violates the team rule that forbids silencing exceptions.

evidence.quote: A failed notification is logged so that operators can see it.
Never silence an exception: catch the narrowest type, and log or re-raise it. `except Exception: pass` is not allowed.

findings.verification_note: The assign method catches any Exception from the notifier and does a bare `pass` with no logging, matching the cited code and violating both the ticket requirement to log failed notifications and the team rule prohibiting silencing exceptions.

limitations: The notifier callable's implementation and downstream handling of the message are not provided, so potential injection or information leakage risks cannot be fully assessed.

run.ticket: TS-5: Notify the assignee on assignment

criteria.text: When a ticket is assigned, the new assignee is notified.
criteria.explanation: The assign method calls the injected notifier with the assignee and a message after assigning the ticket, satisfying the requirement to notify the new assignee.

evidence.quote: self.notifier(assignee, f"Ticket {ticket.id} was assigned to you: {ticket.title}")

criteria.text: If the notification fails, the assignment still succeeds.
criteria.explanation: The notifier call is wrapped in a try/except block that swallows any exception, allowing the assignment to succeed even if notification fails.
